entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter sends his greetings to the believers in Asia Minor and throughout the world, to everyone from among the Gentiles who believed and received this grace, like the Jews who believed, of whom Peter was one. This one precious faith is a grace from Christ, the righteous and holy Saviour of the whole world. In humility Peter joins his old name "Simon," meaning God hears, to his new name "Peter," meaning the rock, and he describes himself as a servant of Christ and not only His apostle, for he does not forget that he was merely an uneducated fisherman, and that it was Christ who raised him up and made him a great apostle.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter's wish for the believers is an abundance of peace and grace through the knowledge of God and of Christ the Redeemer. Here he repeats what Christ Himself said: "And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent" (Jn 17:3).
Encourage everyone you meet with words of grace, love and peace, so that you reassure all amid the troubles of the world.

(2) Spiritual striving (vv. 3-15:) 3 According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue: 4 Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. 5 And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; 6 And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; 7 And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity. 8 For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. 9 But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins. 10 Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall: 11 For so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

12 Wherefore I will not be negligent to put you always in remembrance of these things, though ye know them, and be established in the present truth. 13 Yea, I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance; 14 Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me. 15 Moreover I will endeavour that ye may be able after my decease to have these things always in remembrance.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: When we have come to know Christ and believed in Him, the Holy Spirit grants us every possibility of the spiritual life through the sacraments of the Church. In Baptism we receive a nature inclined to become like God, and He establishes us in it through the Holy Myron; if we sin, He forgives our sins in the sacrament of confession and nourishes us with His most holy Body and Blood; indeed He shepherds and guides us in His Church through the means of grace. And through the calling to life with Christ, God is glorified in us so that we may live by the spiritual virtues.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: Whereby: glory and virtue.
Exceeding great promises: the promises of the Old Testament and the promises of Christ to those who believe in Him, which the Holy Spirit grants them.
Partakers of the divine nature: the new nature that we receive in Baptism, our union with Christ in the sacrament of the Eucharist, and the permanent indwelling of the Holy Spirit in us.

The work of the Holy Spirit in us gives us glory and virtue through the Holy Sacraments, which lift us up to share in God's nature as far as we are able to bear it. By this spiritual elevation in the Christian life we keep away from the evil lusts that corrupt the souls of the people of the world, and we enjoy purity in our lives.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: For this very reason: to receive the spiritual life, the promises and the participation in the divine nature that grace grants us.

If grace gives us the possibilities of life with Christ, then we must respond to it with spiritual striving and diligence, so that our faith produces spiritual conduct and virtues; and as we live by virtue, we experience God and know Him in practice.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: The Apostle continues his discourse on the stages and degrees of the spiritual life, which is a chain in which each link leads to the next, and he says:

To knowledge temperance: when I experience God and love Him, material things become small in my eyes, so I control myself in using them and am content with little of them; that is, I practice temperance toward them.

To temperance patience: and when I control myself in material things, in emotion and in all earthly matters, the ability to be patient and to endure is formed within me, so I am no longer disturbed by any afflictions. To patience godliness: while I am patient in afflictions and restrain myself from desires for God's sake, His mercies and consolations pour out upon me as divine help, which helps me toward a life of godliness with all that it includes: repentance, the fear of God, clinging to Him and delighting in fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: He continues his discourse on the stages of the spiritual life in this chain, and says:

To godliness brotherly kindness: when a person fears God and lives in repentance and a spiritual relationship with Him, he is satisfied with Him, so he is freed from his selfishness and opens himself to others, and is able to build good relationships with them and to encourage them.

To brotherly kindness charity: by speaking kind words and encouraging others, the heart opens in love toward them, and my love for them confirms and increases my love for God and my faith in Him, so I walk in the virtues through which I know God. And so I find that the chain in its end leads back to its beginning, or that any part of it leads to another and makes me grow spiritually.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: These spiritual stages urge a person on with zeal to know God, and his life is filled with spiritual fruits, which are the virtues and the various kinds of service.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: On the other hand, the one who neglects these spiritual steps and the striving in them is described by the Apostle as blind, or at least as having weak spiritual sight, because he has forgotten the grace he received in the renewal of his nature and in leaving his old sins, since he ought to have grown in the new life with God, and his lack of striving exposes him to returning to his old sins.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: The Apostle urges us to stand firm in the faith to which God called us and in which He chose us to be His children, and this by spiritual striving in all the preceding steps, for by this striving and by holding fast to the faith we protect ourselves from falling into various sins or returning to our old evil life.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: He encourages us to hold fast to spiritual striving, because by it we walk in the way of the Kingdom and its gates are opened to us so that we may enjoy eternal happiness.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: Therefore the Apostle Peter does not neglect to remind them of spiritual striving, although they know it and are established in the faith in Christ in whom they live, because this reminder makes them grow in spiritual striving.

entries.section: (1) The apostolic greeting

paragraphs.text: The Apostle sees that he is responsible to remind them of spiritual striving because he feels that his life on earth is drawing to its end. He compares his life to a dwelling or tent whose removal is near, so that he may move to another place, which is the blessed eternity, and he charges his children not to be negligent in their striving after he leaves them and goes to Christ.

Be careful in your striving against your favorite sin, and know that any effort you offer is precious to God, and He will support you in it so that you experience it in practice, in addition to your being freed from your sin.

entries.section: (3) The Transfiguration and the prophecies prove the divinity of Christ

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter declares that he did not base his preaching on fables he had heard or on stories that men had invented, but that he had himself beheld the power of Christ and His divinity in His life on earth and in events that show His divinity, such as His transfiguration on the mountain.

entries.section: (3) The Transfiguration and the prophecies prove the divinity of Christ

paragraphs.text: Excellent: the highest.

The Apostle Peter affirms the divinity of Christ and His greatness by the glory and honor He received at the Transfiguration, when the Father called to Him from heaven, where the great glory is, saying to Him, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 17:5). Peter, together with James and John, heard the voice of the Father from heaven when they were with Christ on the mount of the Transfiguration.

entries.section: (3) The Transfiguration and the prophecies prove the divinity of Christ

paragraphs.text: A light that shineth: he compares the prophecies to a shining lamp.
A dark place: the Old Testament, when humanity was far from God and from knowing Him.

The day ... the day star: Christ, when He became incarnate in the fullness of time so that the prophecies would be fulfilled in Him. He directs their attention to the prophecies about Christ in the Old Testament that prove His divinity; they are like the light of God in the midst of the darkness of humanity's ignorance in the Old Testament, until they were fulfilled in Christ by His Incarnation and redemption.

entries.section: (3) The Transfiguration and the prophecies prove the divinity of Christ

paragraphs.text: What the prophets recorded in their prophecies was not a human effort to interpret events, but was by inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (3) The Transfiguration and the prophecies prove the divinity of Christ

paragraphs.text: No prophecy ever came by the will of man, and these prophets did not speak from themselves or according to their own inclinations, but spoke moved by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.
Read the words of the Holy Bible with reverence, knowing that they are the voice of God to you, that you may live by it and apply it in your daily life.
The false teachers

entries.section: (1) The appearance of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter reminds them of the false prophets who misled the kings and the people in the Old Testament so that they would not listen to the words of God's prophets, as happened in the days of King Ahab (1 Kgs 22:22). Likewise now there are false teachers who proclaim heresies by which they reject the divinity of Christ, who bought us with His blood; so they and those who follow them are far from salvation, and nothing awaits them but eternal torment.

entries.section: (1) The appearance of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: These false teachers claim to be Christians although their doctrine is mistaken, so they mislead many of the people and lead them to destruction, and because of these heresies they confuse the thoughts of the pagans about Christianity, so that they speak evil of it.

entries.section: (1) The appearance of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: They trade in souls, despising the precious blood that was shed for them, and deceive the hearts of the simple with kind words and smooth, deceitful speech; therefore judgment pursues them, and their destruction does not delay or slumber.

Be careful about what you hear or read, and if you find it different from what you have learned in the Church, be on your guard and ask your father of confession, so that you are not led astray by strange teachings that resemble the sound teachings.

entries.section: (2) The punishment of the wicked

paragraphs.text: The Apostle makes clear the justice of God, who punishes those who persist in their wickedness, such as the false teachers. And he gives three examples of His justice:

The first example: His punishment in ancient times of the angels who became proud and fell and were sentenced to eternal torment; He bound them and prevented them from returning to their first rank and from enjoying fellowship with Him, and they are now awaiting their eternal torment. If His mercy did not prevent His justice toward the fallen angels, then it does not prevent His punishing the heretics either.
Chains of darkness: the bonds of their sin, which prevent them from enjoying fellowship with God.
Hell: the place where the wicked wait, but they can war against human beings with God's permission.
Reserved: waiting and bound, not enjoying the sight of God until the day of judgment comes. Judgment: the day of judgment, which transfers them to eternal torment.

entries.section: (2) The punishment of the wicked

paragraphs.text: The second example of God's justice is that He spared not the old world in the days of Noah, who preached righteousness and they did not respond to him, so God brought a flood upon them because of their ungodliness; yet He preserved Noah, who was one of eight persons who were saved from the flood, namely he, his wife, his three sons and their wives.

entries.section: (2) The punishment of the wicked

paragraphs.text: The third example of His justice is His sentence of destruction upon the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah because their wickedness had increased and the cup of their iniquities was full; so He turned them into ashes, making them an example to everyone who lives an ungodly life in every generation and persists in evil without repenting.

entries.section: (2) The punishment of the wicked

paragraphs.text: Alongside God's justice, His mercy appears in His care for His children; He did not forget Lot and his two daughters, because he did not mingle with the wicked in their uncleanness, but was greatly distressed by the conduct of these wicked people.

entries.section: (2) The punishment of the wicked

paragraphs.text: For as Lot, a righteous man, dwelt among them, his soul was grieved every day by the shameful perversions in their conduct, which he saw and heard of.

entries.section: (2) The punishment of the wicked

paragraphs.text: He concludes from the preceding verses that God is able to deliver His righteous children from the afflictions of life and to keep them in their upright faith, whereas the wicked He puts in hell, the place where the wicked wait until the day of judgment, to enter into eternal torment. For God is perfect in His mercy to His children and in His justice toward the wicked.

Do not despise God's longsuffering and mercy and so persist in your sins, but use it for repentance and for staying away from sources of evil, for your attempts at repentance are very precious in God's eyes however weak you are, and He is ready to support you and, in the end, to lift your sins from you.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: Dominion: the Lord Christ and the authority of the Church represented in the Apostles and their successors the bishops. Dignities: the angels.
The Apostle declares that God's punishment is severe for the false teachers, who have evil characteristics, the most important of which are:
1- Uncleanness: by being carried away into the lusts of the flesh and evil sexual perversions.

2- Pride: they rise up with their heresies against Christ Himself and against the Church, her shepherds and her teachers, proclaiming strange ideas; they are bold in ungodliness and evil, and boast of their pride to the point of speaking evil words against the angels.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: The righteousness of the angels appears in their not condemning the demons or these heretics, since they leave judgment to God, and we ought to imitate them.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: 3- Ignorance: he compares them to unreasoning, predatory beasts, made to be caught and killed by men, for these false teachers have sunk to a rank lower than the animals, instead of preserving their rational human dignity. And although they are ignorant of the angels, they invent judgments and slanders about what they do not know; so just as the unreasoning animals perish, they too perish like them, and the cause of their destruction is not outside them but is their own corruption.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: 4- Delight in lusts: the false teachers are occupied with material desires and take pleasure in them, although they are temporary and are followed by eternal punishment, and they are also characterized by many other evil traits such as vanity.
5- Hypocrisy: they pretend to be godly and take part in the love feasts with the members of the Church and try to cause them to stumble with their mistaken ideas.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: 6- The evil gaze: because their hearts are full of uncleanness, their eyes look about seeking defilement, so they are adulterous eyes.
7- Deceit: they are not content with doing evil, but try to influence the simple and unstable in order to deceive and mislead them.

8- Covetousness: they have fallen into the love of possessing and are absorbed in lusts with all their hearts. And since they have these evil characteristics, God's punishment, His curses and eternal destruction come upon them.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: 9- Love of money: these false teachers were members of the Church who walked uprightly, but they loved their lusts and perversions, so they sought material things, like the prophet Balaam, who loved material gain and caused the children of Israel to stumble so that they departed from God and their enemies defeated them (Num 22-25).

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: The ignorance of the false teachers appears like that of Balaam, who was warned to turn back from his evil by his donkey, which spoke with a human voice to rebuke him (Num 22:28-30).

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: A tempest: violent winds.
The blackness of darkness: intense darkness.

He affirms the hypocrisy of these wicked people, comparing them to wells to which the thirsty person comes and finds no water in them, or to clouds that the farmer waits for to rain and water his crops, but the winds drive them away and he benefits nothing from them. And he states again that after this life eternal destruction awaits them, which is expressed by intense darkness.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: The great things of falsehood: innovations and heresies.
10- Varied stumbling blocks: they proclaim many heresies, and whoever of the believers rejects them, they try to bring down into unclean lusts and fornication in order to draw him away from God.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: 11- False freedom: they imagine that indulgence in lusts is freedom, and in misleading others they promise them this false freedom, but in truth it is slavery to sin. And if they are slaves to sin, how can they free others, since they themselves first need to repent of their sins in order to be truly free?

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: 12- Returning to sin: these false teachers received purity when they believed in Christ and left behind their former evil lusts, but they returned to them and plunged even more deeply into them, so that the last end of their life is worse than before their faith, because after they were enlightened they rejected Christ and preferred evil.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: Their knowledge of the new life in Christ condemns them. Had they not known it, they would have some excuse, but now their judgment is greater.

entries.section: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

paragraphs.text: He quotes a verse from the Book of Proverbs (Prov 26:11), comparing the false teachers to a dog that vomits and then, after being cleaned, returns again to its vomit, so it remains filthy and no one can come near it because of its smell and its repulsive appearance. He also compares them to the swine, which after being washed returns to its bad habit of wallowing in the black mire, so that its whole body becomes dirty. So these wicked people return to their evils as if they did not know Christ or the pure life that is in Him.

God accepts your repentance however great your sins, but do not be negligent and return to the encouragements of sin and forget all the blessings you received in life with God; remember the judgment and the eternal torment that await the wicked, so that you flee from sin.
Faith in God and readiness for His second coming

entries.section: (1) The purpose of the epistle

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter makes clear that this is his second epistle, and that its purpose, together with the first epistle, is to remind them of God's commandments, to care for their spiritual life, and to remember the second coming of Christ. The kindness of the Apostle Peter appears in praising the readers of the epistle by describing their minds as pure, which encourages them to give attention to his words and to accept them.

entries.section: (1) The purpose of the epistle

paragraphs.text: The commandments with which the Apostle Peter reminds them are the teachings of the prophets in the Old Testament and the commandments of Christ in the New Testament.

Praise the one you are speaking to, so that you open his heart to hear your words, especially if it is a reproach or a rebuke, and know that words of praise, before they give rest to those who hear you, give rest and joy to you yourself.

entries.section: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

paragraphs.text: He warns of the appearance of unbelieving people in the last days, by which he means the period from the days of Christ until His second coming; they are people immersed in their lusts, who scoff arrogantly at God and His Church.

entries.section: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

paragraphs.text: These wicked people reject the idea of the second coming of Christ, on the evidence that the earth and all that is on it has remained steady over the years, so it will not perish or change as Christ said at His second coming; indeed all the fathers and forefathers have died and the earth and all that is on it has not changed.

entries.section: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter answers those who do not believe in the coming of Christ with these proofs:

1- Creation: the heavens and the earth did not exist, and God created them by His word out of the water that filled every place; then God divided between waters and waters and made the heavens above, and then caused the dry land to appear in the midst of the waters, and it became earth (Gen 1:9, 10); and as God created them, He is able to remove and change them at His second coming.

entries.section: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

paragraphs.text: Whereby: the heavens and the earth.

2- The Flood: the second proof of the coming of Christ and the change of the heavens and the earth is that in the days of the Flood the fountains of the great deep burst forth from the earth and the windows of heaven were opened with abundant rain, so that the whole world and humanity were drowned (Gen 7:11).

entries.section: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

paragraphs.text: But the present heavens and earth will also be kept by the word of the Lord until the day of judgment, when God will destroy the ungodly.

entries.section: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

paragraphs.text: 3- Time: he offers a third proof of the necessity of the second coming of Christ, which is that time for us as human beings is measured and we consider it short or long, so we say that many years have passed since the creation of the world and nothing has changed; but with God there is no time, rather a thousand years equal a day, as the same meaning is stated in the Psalm (Ps 90:4), and therefore His promise of His second coming will surely be fulfilled however long the time may be.

entries.section: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

paragraphs.text: What people think is slowness on God's part, so that they doubted His word and its fulfillment, is in truth longsuffering on His part, to give a greater opportunity for repentance so that He may save all His children from destruction.

entries.section: (2) The denial of the second coming of Christ and the answer to it

paragraphs.text: He declares an important truth, which is that the day of judgment will come suddenly, as a thief attacks to steal without anyone knowing the time of his attack. On that day there will be mighty sounds, which he calls a great noise, and the elements that compose the different materials will be dissolved and burn up, just as it was scientifically established in the twentieth century that the atom can be split. And the earth will burn, just as some nations have been able to cause huge fires with modern destructive bombs, and the heavens will burn, with the various planets they contain. By the heavens is not meant, of course, the throne of God, but the heaven of the planets.
Do not let your mind doubt the word of God, for faith is higher than reason. Try to understand with your mind, but do not oppose the word of God in the Holy Bible.

entries.section: (3) Preparation for the second coming

paragraphs.text: Since the heavens and the earth will be dissolved and changed, the Apostle calls us to prepare for the second coming of the Lord by the following:

1- Holy conversation: that is, walking in righteousness and purity and carrying out God's commandments, knowing that our life is holy and consecrated to Him, so we are not occupied with the evils of the world.

entries.section: (3) Preparation for the second coming

paragraphs.text: 2- Longing for the Kingdom: because the heavens and the earth will burn, that is, pass away, we do not cling to material things but long to depart from the prison of the body, because we cannot be content with fellowship with Him on earth and yearn to enjoy permanent presence with Him in the Kingdom.

entries.section: (3) Preparation for the second coming

paragraphs.text: 3- Hope: although the world is full of evil and we strive to hold fast to righteousness amid its evils, we have hope in the Kingdom of Heaven, in which there is nothing but righteousness.

entries.section: (3) Preparation for the second coming

paragraphs.text: 4- Purity: we prepare by purifying our hearts from the attachments of the world, so that we gain inner peace and Christ dwells in us, in preparation for His permanent and complete dwelling in the Kingdom.

entries.section: (3) Preparation for the second coming

paragraphs.text: 5- Making use of life: our life is an opportunity that God gives us by His longsuffering to repent of our sins and do good in preparation for the Kingdom, as the Apostle Paul affirmed these same meanings so that we may prepare for the Kingdom (1 Thess 5:6), (1 Thess 4:13-18), (1 Cor 51-58).

entries.section: (3) Preparation for the second coming

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter points out that the epistles of the Apostle Paul contain philosophical statements that some wicked people distort and interpret wrongly, leading to the destruction of their souls; therefore it is necessary to adhere to the Church's interpretation of the epistles of Paul and of the whole Holy Bible, and no one should rush into an interpretation of his own, lest he go astray.

entries.section: (3) Preparation for the second coming

paragraphs.text: 6- Guarding against error: that is, the deviant teachings of the false teachers, and submission to the Church so that we stand firm in the upright faith that we learned and came to know from her.

entries.section: (3) Preparation for the second coming

paragraphs.text: 7- Spiritual growth: caring about spiritual growth in the knowledge of Christ through the Holy Bible and all the teachings of the Church, and experiencing Him through prayers, spiritual striving and service.

Remember always that you will leave this life, so prepare for eternity by caring for your prayers and readings every day, and if you sin, hasten to repentance, so that you enjoy the vision of God always.
